round16_result.summary: 6/16 byte-exact, each with its own _solved.cpp and a re-run proof showing exact_match true, boundary_agreement true, 0 differing words

001053c0.mechanism: three calls then the global is cleared; the target loads the global TWICE, so it must be declared volatile

0014cfc8.mechanism: three calls then two global clears in the same page, each with its own lui; declaring BOTH globals volatile keeps the two lui/store pairs ordered as the target has them

00197be8.mechanism: global loaded once into s0 and forwarded to both calls; the trailing empty asm inside the guard block keeps the second call a real jal

001c13a8.mechanism: three real calls; the load of param_1[12] must NOT be hoisted above the first call, so it is written inline as an argument rather than into a temporary

001e6c00.mechanism: two calls; the second needs a trailing empty asm, and the global is reached by lw so the TRUNCATING no-carry rule applies - declare 0x1dae6e4, not Ghidra's 0x1de6e4

002d47a8.mechanism: vtable-pointer store then two calls; the +3208 argument must be spelled as a BYTE offset, not a u32 index, or GCC folds it to +802

0014dbc8.best: v01 (6 words); v02 volatile, v03 barrier (5 words)
0014dbc8.blocker: the target orders the six zero-stores sb 0x1d9, sw 0x1d0, sh 0x1d4, sb 0x1d6, sb 0x1d7, sb 0x1d8; GCC swaps the first two (emits 0x1d8 then 0x1d9). All six are to the same base, so there is no aliasing reason for the swap and neither a memory barrier nor volatile pins it.
attempts: memory barrier after the leading byte store

0014dc08.best: v01 (6 words); v02 volatile, v03 barrier (5 words)

00170530.blocker: the target keeps the two constants in DISTINCT registers (li t6,1; sh t7,58; sb t6,0); GCC reuses t7 for both. param_3 must stay unmasked (a u16 parameter adds an andi, 8 words). Barriers and named temporaries both widen the gap.
attempts: u32 parameter with memory barriers between stores

002e2e18.blocker: the machine form is a LIKELY branch (beql) with lw v0,264(s0) in its delay slot and the same load repeated after the call. __builtin_expect plus a volatile reload grew the body to 64/56 instead of producing the likely-branch shape.

0016e200.blocker: two differences: the target uses lq t0/sq t0 where GCC picks t7, and the target emits ld s0,0(sp) TWICE (beq delay slot, then after the sq) while GCC elides the dead reload

00315678.blocker: PROLOGUE-SINK CLASS. The target sinks the vtable-pointer store to the incoming parameter BELOW both prologue saves (sd s0,0(sp); sd ra,8(sp); sw t7,0(a0)); GCC always schedules it BETWEEN them. Same shape as round-15's 0028b7f8.

00265740.blocker: the target is 15 words: it saves ra BEFORE s0 (sd ra,8(sp); sd s0,0(sp)) and ends with sltiu v0,v0,1, i.e. it returns 1 when (x ^ 0x8d) == 0. v02 with the == 0 predicate regressed to 56/60 and sltu; v01's prologue order also differs by one slot, so both the predicate and the prologue ordering are needed at once and no single spelling produced both.

new_compiler_level_classes: prologue-sink: a vtable-pointer store to the incoming parameter is always scheduled BETWEEN the two prologue saves (4 targets now: 0028b7f8 r15, 00315678/00315700/00316890 r16)
